subject: Revised asset map — RoboRide accelerant incorporated. Compensation conversation: three-day deadline.
content: Patricia — I am attaching a revised draft of the three-tier assessment. I updated it this morning after the RoboRide pricing news. The short version: the timeline I had at 18-to-24 months for meaningful ownership attrition compresses to 9-to-12. The $0.12/mile residential coverage with an 8-minute wait is the marginal buyer exit event I had modeled as a future scenario. It is happening now. The tier-one argument — service lane as the non-negotiable core — is stronger than it was a week ago, not weaker. I also added a sub-section on delivery fleet vehicle service demand, which is a potential upside channel we have not discussed. Tier-two showroom projections are revised downward consistent with sector index data at 79. I need two things before I finalize this document: your confirmation that the revised timeline reflects your planning horizon, and a direct conversation about my formal engagement status and compensation. That conversation has been deferred twice. I am not delivering the final assessment without it. I am not saying that as pressure — I am saying it as someone who has been working without a contract for eleven days on a document that is going to shape Q2 decisions. I will be available Thursday and Friday. Tell me when works.

secondary_transaction.subject: Direct floor conversation — service lane capacity and Carlos's read
secondary_transaction.content: Rick calls Carlos directly — not as GM, not in any formal capacity, just as the person who knows the floor. He asks Carlos two things: how is the service lane actually running right now (honest numbers, not what goes on a report), and is Carlos hearing anything from other shops — poaching, offers, anything. Rick tells Carlos enough to make the conversation feel mutual: he is working on a document for Patricia that argues the service lane is the survival core of whatever this dealership becomes, and Carlos is named in it as the irreplaceable anchor of that operation. He wants Carlos to know that before the document is finalized, not after.
secondary_transaction.tone: direct, peer-to-peer, not managerial — Rick is not Carlos's boss right now and he knows it

expected_response: Patricia acknowledges the revised timeline and agrees to a compensation conversation with a specific time. Carlos gives his honest read on service lane status and his own intentions.
tone: professional, direct, non-deferential — this is a negotiation, not a status report
